transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood CSM), Jordan (CTO, Lumos), Samir (Product), Taylor (SRE), Renee (Security), Eli (Finance)

Summary: QBR/Q2 health check focused on usage/cost, reliability incident on 2026-06-28, and roadmap for model rollouts.

00:00 Alex Moreno: hey everyone thanks for carving the time for the QBR. we'll run through usage, incidents, cost, and then roadmap. quick check, everyone can hear me?
00:07 Jordan Reyes: yeah can hear you, thanks Alex.
00:12 Marta Klein: hi all, thanks for joining.
00:15 Priya Desai: hi - Priya here, SE, gonna walk through the performance bits mid-call.
00:22 Eli Brooks: quick note from finance, want to understand the cost uptick on embeddings this quarter.

02:05 Alex Moreno: ok first slide, high level usage. tokens per minute and embedding calls have increased ~2.7x since April, embeddings are driving about 60% of cost increase. we saw a couple of high-traffic routes - search-similarity and inbox-rerank.
02:38 Samir Patel: yeah we pushed vector search to more users in May which explains some of that. the embeddings calls are fairly small but frequent.
03:02 Alex Moreno: got it. on the cost side, some quick levers are moving to batching, enabling prefix/KV cache on responses, and quantization on the model serving side - we can show projected cost savings with Redwood Optimize.
03:20 Eli Brooks: when you say quantization, is that something you do in the hosted cluster or would we need to change our model artifacts?
03:29 Priya Desai: good q - we do server-side quant profiles for compatible open models, for private deployments we can also give recommendations. sometimes artifacts need to be converted but we handle most of that as part of model onboarding; there's a small accuracy tradeoff we quantify.

05:00 Taylor Nguyen: there was an incident June 28th where latency spiked for ~20 minutes. can you walk through what triggered it and remediation?
05:12 Priya Desai: yeah on June 28 we saw a combination of a tail latency event plus increased concurrent KV cache miss rate when a big rerank job started. runtime autoscaling lagged a touch on that pool - we fanned up more nodes but there was a short fall-through. we rolled a hotfix to improve scaling thresholds and added more aggressive pre-warming for scheduled jobs.
05:45 Jordan Reyes: ok that matches our logs; we lost 3% of requests timed out, customer-facing impact was small but noticeable. what SLA changes should we consider?
06:00 Alex Moreno: for production-critical routes we recommend Redwood Dedicated with fixed GPU pools to get guaranteed throughput and more stable tail latencies. we also offer burst capacity and can configure canary rollouts.
06:20 Taylor Nguyen: can Dedicated integrate with our VPC and KMS? we need keys managed by our HSM and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
06:31 Marta Klein: yes - Dedicated and Private both support customer-managed KMS/HSM, VPC peering, and audit log forwarding. we'll also share our SOC2 report and pen test summary.
06:52 Renee Gomez: on compliance, we need data residency for PHI, and proof that logs don't contain sensitive tokens. is there redaction or token masking?
07:10 Priya Desai: we have token-level redaction options, and can deploy a private control plane for regulated workloads - that keeps metadata in your VPC. we'll include redaction configs in the security pack.

09:00 Alex Moreno: ok next, roadmap. Lumos plans to roll out a secure patient-chat feature in Q4 which will need lower latency and PHI controls. recommended path: start PoC on Redwood Dedicated in staging, run benchmarks for latency and cost, then evaluate Private/on-prem for production if needed.
09:26 Samir Patel: timeline wise, we want staging by September, production by November. can you support that?
09:34 Priya Desai: timeline is doable. we'd want a 4-6 week PoC: week 1 onboarding and model tuning, week 2 performance benchmarks (latency and throughput), week 3 cost optimization and caching, week 4 docs and runbook.

11:15 Eli Brooks: finance will likely push for a committed discount if we do dedicated. can you provide committed pricing examples?
11:22 Alex Moreno: yes - we'll send a reserved capacity quote with multiple commitment tiers and projected unit costs. we'll include a comparison: hosted on-demand vs 6/12 month reserved.

12:40 Jordan Reyes: any blockers on our side? we need to line up security review and have our compliance team sign off on SOC2 and KMS details.
12:52 Marta Klein: i'll share the security pack (SOC2 attestation, network diagrams, KMS architecture, pen test summary).
13:05 Renee Gomez: great, also need details on RBAC and SSO - we use Okta and need SCIM provisioning.
13:12 Priya Desai: SCIM/SSO/SAML are supported, RBAC roles can be mapped to your groups; we'll include config examples.

14:45 Alex Moreno: on the technical side, Priya, can you summarize the recommended config for the rerank and similarity routes?
14:52 Priya Desai: sure - for rerank: keep a smaller model with quantization, enable KV cache for repeated prefixes, set batch window to 20-50ms for balancing latency and throughput. for similarity/embeddings: use microbatching, sticky routing to same GPU pool to warm cache, and use dedicated pool if you hit sustained high QPS. also consider using compensated fallbacks to smaller models for tail cases.
15:30 Taylor Nguyen: sticky routing meaning route by customer id or request hash?
15:35 Priya Desai: request hash or user id is typical; it reduces cold KV cache misses.

17:00 Samir Patel: curious about RBAC and audit logs retention - can we keep logs for 12 months for SOC audits?
17:09 Marta Klein: yes, audit log retention can be configured; long-term retention is an add-on we can enable.

18:00 Alex Moreno: ok let's talk numbers briefly - current monthly spend $86k, embeddings ~52k of that. with initial optimizations (batching + caching) we project 25-40% reduction on embedding cost; with reserved capacity + quant we can target ~50% reduction in unit cost depending on model.
18:25 Eli Brooks: that's promising - will want the detailed worksheet you referenced.
18:30 Alex Moreno: will send.

20:00 Jordan Reyes: any technical debt or migration pains we should expect if we move to Dedicated?
20:10 Priya Desai: minimal; we replicate routes and model versions. main tasks: network setup (VPC peering, firewall rules), model sync and validation, and e2e perf tests. we have a migration checklist.

22:30 Samir Patel: about model versions - can we pin to a specific model release to avoid regressions?
22:36 Priya Desai: yes, version pinning and rollouts (canary/A-B) are supported in the console. we can also set automatic fallback policies to older variants if regressions detected.

24:00 Renee Gomez: one more on encryption: is in-flight TLS with mutual auth supported?
24:08 Marta Klein: yes - mTLS is supported for inter-service and customer connections for Private deployments; for hosted we support TLS and customer-managed VPN for extra isolation.

26:00 Alex Moreno: final recaps and next steps. we'll send: 90-day usage + cost by route, reserved capacity pricing, security pack, and schedule the SE deep-dive for benchmarking.
26:18 Jordan Reyes: sounds good. can you prioritize the security pack this week? that's the gating item for our compliance review.
26:28 Marta Klein: yes sending by 2026-07-15.

28:00 Priya Desai: i'll include a sample benchmark plan focusing on KV cache miss scenarios and batching windows; we'll test both hosted and dedicated configurations.

30:00 Eli Brooks: finance will need committed pricing by next Friday to make procurement timelines.
30:08 Alex Moreno: we'll include a 6- and 12-month quote and an illustrative TCO.

32:00 Jordan Reyes: ok thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness.
32:10 Samir Patel: quick question - do you have any references for other healthcare customers doing PHI workloads?
32:18 Marta Klein: we can provide redacted references and a case study where a customer moved to Dedicated for PHI. will include in the pack.

34:00 Alex Moreno: any other questions?
34:05 Taylor Nguyen: none from SRE.
34:10 Renee Gomez: no, thanks.

35:00 Alex Moreno: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
35:10 Jordan Reyes: thanks, bye.
35:12 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels auto-generated, occasional word swaps (KV cache pronounced k-v cash), minor punctuation issues.
